content.title: Wisconsin hockey scores 2-1 win over North Dakota to advance to NCAA championship game
content.text: Updated April 9, 2026, 8:48 p.m. CTLAS VEGAS – The Wisconsin hockey team is one win away from raising another banner to rafters of the Kohl Center.The Badgers defeated No. 1 seed North Dakota in the NCAA Tournament, 2-1, Thursday, April 9 in a national semifinal at T-Mobile Arena.Wisconsin (24-12-3) will face the winner of the Michigan-Denver semifinal at 4:30 p.m. Saturday, April 11. That game between the Wolverines and Pioneers will be played later Thursday evening.A strong start made the difference for the Badgers. Senior Simon Tassy and sophomore Ryan Botterill scored first period goals for UW. The defense did the rest.BOX SCORE:Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 1The Badgers killed five penalties and didn’t allow a goal until the final minute when the Fighting Hawks pulled their goalie.Wisconsin freshman goaltender Daniel Hauser finished with 21 saves against the nation's No. 3 scoring team.Check jsonline.com here throughout the afternoon and evening for updates. Postgame with Wisconsin's Ryan BotterillThe Badgers sophomore explained the impact of the team's fast start and the connect with Ben Dexheimer that led to his first period goal. Postgame with Wisconsin's Simon TassyThe Badgers senior explained what led to his first period goal and gave his thoughts on playing for a national championship Saturday. Oliver Tulk, Daniel Hauser makes highlight reel with hustle playThis diving effort by Oliver Tulk came during the waning moments of the second period. Yet another PK for the BadgersWisconsin has drawn four penalties this evening, but none have come back to haunt the team.Luke Osburn was hit an a tripping penalty at the 5:32 mark of the third period. The result? One shot on goal for the Fighting Hawks, one shot block and two attempts that were off target.Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0, 12 minutes left in regulation. Tale of the tape after second periodScore: Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0Shots: Wisconsin 25, North Dakota 16Saves: Wisconsin 16, North Dakota 23Faceoffs: Wisconsin 23, North Dakota 17Power plays: Wisconsin 0-1, North Dakota 0-3 Another successful PK for WisconsinThe Badgers' penalty kill came through for the second time in the second period. This time UW played with two men down for 1 minutes 57 seconds after Joe Palodichuk followed Luke Osburn to the box.Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0, 2 minutes left in second period Wisconsin penalty kill delivers Killing penalties hasn’t been a strength of the Badgers this season, but the unit shut down North Dakota’s first power play of the evening.Ben Dexheimer drew a holding penalty with 10:46 left in the second period. Over the next 2 minutes the Badgers pushed the Fighting Hawks out of their zone three times though they got three shots on goal.Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0, with 8 1/2 minutes to go in second period. Ryan Botterill's goal was his 10th of the seasonWhen Ryan Botterlill scored at the 13:21 mark of the first period, it was his 10th goal of the season.Ben Dexheimer's pass through the neutral zone set up Botterill for the opportunity. A look at the Badgers' first goalSimon Tassy scored the goal, but Vasily Zelenov's hustle and work on the boards made the play happen. Wisconsin-North Dakota tale of the tape after one period Score: Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0Shots: Wisconsin 18, North Dakota 4Saves: Wisconsin 4, North Dakota 16Faceoffs: Wisconsin 15, North Dakota 8Power plays: Wisconsin 0-1, North Dakota 0-0 Goals by Simon Tassy, Ryan Botterill give UW 2-0 leadThe Badgers were pushing the tempo of the game during the first 12 minutes. They were finally rewarded with a two-goal outburst in 27 seconds.Simon Tassy got the first score a the 12:54 mark of the period. Vasily Zelenov, who beat a North Dakota player to the corner for the puck, made the pass for the assist, hatting Tassy has he charged into the zone.Ryan Botterill did the honors at the 13:21 mark, depositing a pass from Ben Dexheimer to push the lead to 2-0Wisconsin 2, North Dakota 0, 5 minutes left in first period. No score but plenty of chances for UWWe’re scoreless with 8:51 left in the first period, but the Badgers are dictating the game. UW owns a 9-3 edge in shots on goalOn the other end of the ice, goaltender Daniel Hauser has made three nifty saves to keep the Fighting Hawks off the board.Wisconsin 0, North Dakota 0, 8:51 left in first period How the Badgers, Fighting Hawks are lining up The Badgers make grand entrance to Frozen FourAbout 2 1/2 hours before the start of the national semifinal, Wisconsin arrived at the arena. Captain Ben Dexheimer led the procession.How to watch Wisconsin hockey in the Frozen FourTV channel: ESPN2Stream: The game is available on the ESPN app and Fubo, which has a free trial for new subscribersHow to listen to Wisconsin vs North Dakota on the radioRadio: AM-920 WOKY plus a statewide network.What are Wisconsin’s odds of winning the national championship?BetMGM lists Michigan as the favorite to win the title, and the Badgers rank last out of the four semifinalists as of Thursday morning.The third-seeded Badgers are the lowest seed in a field that includes No. 1 seeds Michigan and North Dakota and No. 2 seed Denver, which is making its third straight Frozen Four appearance.If Wisconsin is embracing the underdog role, it wasn’t apparent Wednesday, April 9. “We're just trying to focus on ourselves and cross those Ts and dot our Is, just sticking to our dailies and worrying about how we can improve our game and how we're going to bring it tomorrow,” senior Jack Horbach said. “I think we don't really look at ourselves as underdogs, but I think we're ready to play when we punch through the drop tomorrow.”A first for the Frozen FourThe Badgers aren’t the only team in the national semifinals with a freshman goaltender. Every team is starting one, a first in the history of the Frozen Four.Here is what UW coach Mike Hastings said about his netminder, Daniel Hauser.“This one, in that locker room, whether we've won, we've lost, he's crushed it; he's had a rough night, he just kind of stays even keel,” Hastings said. “And I'm going to tell you, as a coach, you respect that.”
